parsed.explanation: Combined secular 10-14 year criminalisation and northern Sharia death-penalty exposure for same-sex acts, documented as a police lever against visibly gender-nonconforming people: torture, arbitrary arrests, mass hotel raids, extortion and a beating for 'looking gay'. A trans woman's 2024 killing produced no charges after six months, custody placement is discretionary with a max-security case found unlawful, and there are no legal protections. Dating-app luring and outing blackmail, fear of care/reporting, and discretionary detention make outing potentially catastrophic, especially in the north; presentation-specific law is not established as enacted. Severity and state perpetration dominate, offset only by absence of documented capital prosecution for presentation alone.

entry_documents.exposure: Up to 14 years under secular law; death penalty for male same-sex acts in 12 northern states/provinces. Travel warning cites attacks, blackmail, intimidation.
entry_documents.interaction: Document/appearance mismatch can trigger police stops, raids and extortion under the same-sex law, exposing visitor to secular or northern religious penalties depending on location.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented police torture, arbitrary arrests, multi-year pre-trial detention, mass arrests, and discretionary max-security placement of a prominent trans woman in 2024, ruled unlawful for a first-time offender.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for perceived sexuality/presentation can become prolonged detention with beating, extortion and discretionary birth/case-by-case placement, with no recorded protection outcome.

care_services.exposure: Many LGBTQ+ people fear seeking medical care due to arrest and extortion risk; community health work hampered by the act.
care_services.interaction: Emergency or routine care discovery can lead to reporting, extortion or arrest rather than treatment continuity; no documented visitor care protection.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2014 act bans cohabitation, public same-sex affection and organisations, 10-14 years; described as weaponised, fuelling violence, extortion and discrimination. Cross-dressing criminalisation proposed, enactment not established.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Law provides cover for police abuse and private extortion; northern religious law adds death-penalty layer. No enacted trans-specific protection offsets it.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Beaten trans woman found dead August 2024; police misgendered her as 'a man fully dressed in female clothing'; no suspect charged six months later. Police themselves beat and extort people perceived as gay.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are both perpetrators and non-responsive investigators, so street violence and app-lure beatings/filming/blackmail have no documented remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No legal protections for LGBTQ+ people; fear of reporting; investigations without arrests; placement and enforcement frequency undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Nominal constitutional healthcare guarantee does not displace criminalisation; without recourse, all other exposures become unremedied.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: routine police abuse, imprisonment, illusory remedies. Lower than 0.15 would require capital prosecution for presentation itself, not documented here; higher because trans presentation alone is not shown criminalised as enacted.

Lower than 0.25-B: that anchor has short jail/no execution for gender and extortion, whereas here penalties reach 14 years and death in the north, torture and mass raids are documented, and a trans killing remains unprosecuted.

Materially below 0.35-B: there detention rarely becomes imprisonment and lethal force is not credible. Here long imprisonment, torture, death-penalty exposure in part of the country, and impunity for a trans killing are documented.

parsed.synthesis: Exposure is traveller-facing, not merely resident: police use the same-sex statute against those who 'look gay', raid hotels, extort and beat, and dating apps are traps for outing/blackmail. Northern religious law adds a death-penalty tier to the nationwide 14-year regime. Protections are absent - no legal protections, no charges for the 2024 trans killing, discretionary custody, and fear of care/reporting. Interaction is cumulative: outing at a checkpoint, hotel or app meeting can lead to detention, extortion, max-security placement, or worse, with no working remedy. This combined regime sits below the 0.25 anchor, above the execution-for-presentation 0.05 anchor.
